allowed_actions: run healthz readyz and v2 bootstrap smoke
reuse the immutable image and registered ECS task-definition revision from the current workflow
create CodeDeploy AppSpec content in same-job runner temp files
create a CodeDeploy deployment from infra-provided application and deployment group names
run healthz readyz and v2 bootstrap smoke after the deployment succeeds
must_not_own: CodeDeploy application or deployment group topology
blue green target groups or listener topology
CodeDeploy service role or IAM boundary

control_plane_may_own: create CodeDeploy deployment from the public image digest and infra-provided deployment target
run healthz readyz and v2 bootstrap smoke after traffic shift
tighten public workflow redaction without changing AWS topology
infra_must_own: blue green target groups and listener topology
CodeDeploy service role and IAM permission boundary
Terraform drift and operator evidence interpretation

public_repo_should_minimize: publish only stable configuration key names that operators must set
avoid environment-specific examples for domains, clusters, services, applications, deployment groups, ARNs, and URLs
keep live handoff values in same-job runner temp files instead of reusable workflow outputs or artifacts
public_repo_must_not_commit_or_upload: workflow_dispatch input values carrying live URLs
GitHub step outputs carrying live deployment values

infra_consumes.local_scope: Infra owns topology, drift policy, IAM, and operator evidence. It does not own runtime artifact CD execution.

dependency_direction.top_down: Runtime artifact CD behavior changes in control-plane first; infra consumes the required topology/evidence needs.
dependency_direction.bottom_up: Infra may discover topology or security constraints and request a control-plane workflow change, but that does not move CD execution out of control-plane.
